The bumps appear to float slightly rather than clearly originating from or resting on the shelf plane. This is a depth-reading problem — the viewer cannot easily determine whether the peaks emerge from the shelf surface or hover above it. Additionally, the bottom-left construction view, while energetically exploratory, becomes so dense with overlapping lines that the underlying structural logic is difficult to extract — the scaffolding should clarify form, not obscure it.

🛠️ Next Step: Take the bottom-right presentation view and redraw it as a single focused exercise: before drawing any contour, lightly establish the shelf plane as a flat ellipse or rectangle in perspective, then explicitly draw the base of each bump as a small ellipse sitting ON that plane. Only after anchoring each bump's footprint should you draw the rising contour up to the peak. This 'footprint-first' discipline will force the bumps to read as grounded surface features rather than floating forms, and will directly strengthen your ability to communicate surface origin in presentation-quality sketches.
